summary: ObjectGenome v1 defines caster swivelAxis and rollAxis as canonical unit direction vectors, but both current inspect() validation and retained generation-8 PR #395's standalone decoder boundary validate the axes independently and accept a physically degenerate caster whose two axes are parallel. Propose a bounded post-#395 ObjectGenome leaf that rejects non-orthogonal caster axis frames at both semantic boundaries, preserves all shipped fixture identities/fingerprints, performs no adapter-side normalization, and adds deterministic accepted/rejected tolerance regressions. This is distinct from the already proposed ObjectGenome state/cardinality and free-form string budget leaves.
evidence: Docs/OBJECT_GENOME.md defines caster swivelAxis and rollAxis as canonical unit vectors and makes mechanism semantics project-owned so realization adapters do not invent competing physical interpretations; it specifies only the individual magnitude tolerance today.

Retained PR #395 exact head ebfd17e7a2d5cf2083b90e0122b70bc5c39d0962 calls validateAxis() independently for swivelAxis and rollAxis in full inspect(), while standaloneMechanismIsCanonical() independently calls isCanonicalUnitAxis() for each axis; neither checks their dot product or frame relationship.

Current ObjectGenomeFixtures office-chair casters and PhysicsLabObjectGenomes rolling-cart casters both author swivelAxis={0,1,0} and rollAxis={1,0,0}, so an orthogonality fence preserves shipped canonical recipes and requires no fixture identity/fingerprint migration.

Repository PR/issue searches for caster orthogonality found no existing implementation/review leaf; the existing proposed HG-BACKFILL-OBJECTGENOME-STATE-BOUNDS and HG-BACKFILL-OBJECTGENOME-STRING-BUDGET lanes cover different bounded-memory concerns.
